Generally, the centerline of the improved highway is located on the centerline of the present and proposed right-of-way, thus equalizing to a great extent the taking of private property north and south of the improvement. However, in two locations existing features required other alignments. Existing topographic features and facilities were disturbed as little as possible. In the built-up portions of the corridor, the absence of an adequate right-of-way width requires land takings involving both business and residential property.
1. Alignment A
Alignment A locates the road improvement in the middle of the right-of-way, holding the centerline along the east-west section lines throughout the length of the improvement, except in the vicinity of Crawford Avenue where slight shifts are made.
From Cicero Avenue, the western terminus of the proposed project, eastward to Kostner Avenue the proposed improvement follows the existing centerline of Lincoln Highway. Minor land taking only is required in this portion of the project since adequate right-of-way width is presently available throughout most of this section.
From Kostner Avenue eastward to Crawford Avenue the improvement has been swung southward slightly to avoid disturbing an extensive channelization of Butterfield Creek tributary and two presently adequate bridges leading from Lincoln Highway into the Korvette Shopping Center on the north side of the highway.
At the Crawford Avenue/Lincoln Highway/Governor's Highway intersection several alternatives were investigated which both left the intersection as a five-way complex and separated it into two or more right-angled intersections. The recommended alternative shifts Governor's Highway to the north to intersect Crawford Avenue at a right angle opposite the Korvette Shopping Center drive-way and far enough north of Lincoln Highway to provide adequate storage for the large number of vehicles making left turns onto Lincoln Highway. The resulting pair of four-way intersections improve the traffic safety as well as the traffic flow characteristics.
